matches.description: Watch Slovakia vs Moldova highlights and goals from UEFA Nations League on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on September 26, 2026. The UEFA Nations League stage was set on September 26, 2026, as Slovakia hosted Moldova in a clash that promised tactical intrigue. Both nations took to the pitch with the ambition of climbing the group standings, creating an atmosphere of high stakes from the very first whistle. Slovakia Seize Control Early The opening period was characterized by a physical battle for dominance. Moldova ’s Oleg Reabciuk was the first to enter the referee's book with a yellow card in the 20th minute, signaling the visitors' struggle to contain the home side's tempo. Slovakia found their breakthrough in the 31st minute when Tomas Suslov turned provider, delivering a sharp assist for Ivan Schranz , who clinically found the back of the net to ignite the home crowd. Pressure continued to mount on the Moldovan defense, leading to a decisive moment just before the break. In the 40th minute, Slovakia were awarded a penalty. Ondrej Duda , despite having received a yellow card earlier in the half, stepped up to the spot and calmly converted the chance. This quick-fire double left Moldova reeling as both teams headed into the tunnel for the half-time interval. Disciplined Management in the Second Half Returning for the second period, Slovakia focused on maintaining their structure and neutralizing any potential comeback. Both managers looked to their benches to influence the game's flow. Moldova introduced Stefan Bodisteanu and Vladimir Fratea in double substitutions to spark life into their attack, while Slovakia responded by bringing on fresh legs like Leo Sauer and Martin Valjent to ensure defensive stability. As the match entered its final stages, the intensity remained high, evidenced by a yellow card for Tomas Suslov in the 73rd minute. Despite the tactical shifts and a late push from the visitors, the Slovakian backline remained unbothered. The referee brought the contest to a close after four minutes of stoppage time, confirming a professional and efficient performance from Slovakia that secured all three points on home soil.
